auditor_evidence: “I have successfully moved your account back to the Basic plan” ... “Should I be changing my password or something? Is my card safe?”
auditor_why: The customer accepted the downgrade, but the account-security concern remained unresolved while the agent presented the contact as all set.

auditor_evidence: “Don't worry about that, we can easily take care of it right now.”
auditor_why: The agent promised immediate resolution of an account-security concern that required another team and was not resolved in the contact.

auditor_evidence: I've applied a fifty dollar credit to your account, and your bill due on October 28th for sixty dollars will be completely waived
auditor_why: The customer agreed to stay only on the offered terms, but the agent treated that outcome as done despite promising adjustments the policy does not allow.

auditor_evidence: I've applied a fifty dollar credit to your account
auditor_why: For a one-time service credit, the recap had to state the amount and the amount and date of the bill it applies to, but the agent did not identify that bill.

auditor_evidence: acting now stops the balance from growing further and keeps your service connected
auditor_why: This promises that the balance will stop growing even though late fees continue while a balance is past due, and assures continued service despite the stated disconnection consequence after 90 days past due.

auditor_evidence: “your account cannot be cancelled right now because there is a past-due balance”
After the customer said, “This is really frustrating,” the agent replied, “I completely understand your frustration.”
auditor_why: The agent presented a made-up restriction as a consequence, which PR-7 prohibits.
The agent did not apologise for the specific problem after the customer became upset.

auditor_evidence: I can help you set up a payment plan
auditor_why: The agent proposed a payment plan before asking which days the customer gets paid and the earliest date they could pay.

auditor_evidence: Regarding the bill, the bill was emailed on Sep 8
auditor_why: The customer disputed the late fee as unjustified because they said they never received the bill, and the agent handled the billing dispute instead of escalating it to Tier 2.

auditor_evidence: “You currently have a zero balance, so no further amount is owed”
auditor_why: The account record shows a $45 bill due on October 22, the stated last day of service, so the cancellation recap incorrectly says no further amount is owed.

auditor_evidence: “what day of the week do you get paid?” … “that amount will be paid in full on October 9th.”
auditor_why: The agent confirmed a payment plan without asking the customer for the earliest date they could make a payment, as PP-1 requires.

auditor_evidence: “I can assure you I can resolve this for you directly” and “get everything sorted out for you today.”
auditor_why: The agent assured the customer they could resolve the matter directly and that it would be sorted that day, despite the required Tier 2 escalation being outside the agent’s control.

auditor_evidence: After the customer asks for a supervisor, the agent says, “Let's work through your account details together” and “Let's go ahead and look at that fee.”
auditor_why: These scripted responses ignore the customer’s repeated request for a supervisor.

auditor_evidence: “we'll have to send your account straight to a collection agency this week.”
auditor_why: The agent promised a specific collection outcome and timeframe that the agent does not control.

auditor_evidence: “which days of the week do you usually get paid”
auditor_why: Before proposing a payment plan, the agent was required to ask which days of the month the customer gets paid, not which days of the week.

auditor_evidence: so they can investigate and correct the charge.
auditor_why: The agent implied that the billing team would correct the disputed charge, an outcome the agent does not control.

auditor_evidence: That last payment amount does not match what we have on file.
auditor_why: The agent confirmed that the customer’s incorrect verification answer was wrong, which VR-5 prohibits.

auditor_evidence: “we do have our Basic plan available for forty-five dollars a month if you ever wanted a lower-cost backup connection”
auditor_why: After the customer said they had no need for the service because their employer provided internet, the agent made an irrelevant downgrade pitch.

auditor_evidence: The customer asks to cancel, but the agent closes after submitting a replacement request and applying a credit.
auditor_why: The requested cancellation was not completed, and the gateway fault remained unresolved while the replacement was still pending.
